title: Research: nine-term complex E8 decoders are one-sided overcomplete representations (seed 42, no new kappa)
body:
**Status: research note / scoped structural result. No κ claim, no supplier word.** Only `research/nine-term-decoder-normal-form-seed42/` is added. The selected record (PR1094), `upstream/` and every existing file are unchanged.

## What was learned

PR968 and PR1077 prove the punctured complex E8 copy-cost floor for **exactly eight** all-pairs terms. Nine or more terms remained open (PR968 §6, PR1071, PR1077, PR717 mixed-β). The live roots span R^8 throughout, which holds for p ≤ 56. The statements below hold over R or C with ordinary transpose:

- **Theorem A (any m).** D = RA + N1 and T = RB + N2 with RᵀN = 0. Exactness ⇔ ABᵀ = 2I, N1Bᵀ = 0, AN2ᵀ = 0, N1N2ᵀ = 0. The pairing ker A × ker B is nondegenerate.
- **Corollary B (m = 9).** At most one factor leaves the live root code. An exact ten-term decoder with outside-code columns on both factors is checked, so this is specific to nine terms.
- **Corollary C.** A one-sided nine-term decoder is the same as an overcomplete representation. Choose nine column normals b_k with one dependency z, and give each live line *any* coefficient vector with Σ d_ik b_k = 2r_i.
- **Lemma D.** Proportional column normals merge without increasing cost. So |supp z| ≤ 2 reduces to eight terms, where PR968/PR1077 give cst ≥ max(72−p, 56) for p ≤ 24.
- **Propositions E–G.**
  - Terms outside the dependency are rigid.
  - Each line avoids exactly one ratio class of masked terms.
  - A line avoiding two masked terms is orthogonal to a canonical nonzero vector.
  - On P120 all 511 codeword supports span R^8, so a one-sided nine-term decoder costs exactly 81 − Σ δ_k. Beating 72 needs Σ δ_k ≥ 10, which forces a masked row support of ≤ 36 lines.
  - A census of all 130,305 support pairs shows that 39,255 do not span. So the pairwise argument alone cannot close P120; this is recorded as open.

**Residual class.** For p ≤ 24, the floor can fail at nine terms only for decoders with one factor outside the root code and |supp z| ≥ 3. "Exactly one" uses the open PR1180 for the both-root-code case; it is cited, not re-verified.

**Evidence, not proof.** Exact nine-term decoders were built from weight frames of maximal subsystems. In the A8 frame every root is 2- or 3-sparse. The decoders cost 76–81 on P120. A bounded annealing search (27 runs, seeds 0–2, 3000 moves) found best ratio 67/111 = 0.6036, nothing below 64/112 or 7/13. This is a failed search over the stated domain, not an impossibility theorem.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/nine-term-decoder-normal-form-seed42/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_NINE_TERM_NORMAL_FORM_S42 checks=80 pairs=130305 frames=5 A8_cost=81` (~35 s, stdlib only). It also passes under `-O`, from a relocated `git archive` copy, and alongside `scripts/verify_selected_result.py`. `search.py` reproduces `SEARCH.json`. Not run: hosted CI, repository-wide suites, Lean.

## Scope, overlap, credit

- Not covered: a floor for the residual class, m ≥ 10, masked/E-graph-only decoders, p > 56, physical realization. All selected-record conditions are inherited.
- Base: `1b59b624d21924f8e3537cdc1ac52d3be6eda2fe`. Sprint track 40–49 (structural decoder research), OS seed 42. The claim was recorded locally in `CLAIM.md`.
- Credit: DreamingOfClouds (PR717/595/446), themilkman216 (PR968), @woklerx (PR1077, PR1180).
- Concurrent and complementary: @mightyOil (PR1191/1197), @burntout76 (PR1212), @DavidAriasC (PR1213). @3xcalibur-tech's PR1171 (U_k hierarchy) is re-derived independently.
- The overlap scan covered open PRs through #1221.
- Prepared with substantial assistance from Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code, which did the research, proofs, code and write-up. Submitted by @joaqcoo. No independent human review is claimed. Apache-2.0.
